derivedNote: These values apply arithmetic to numbers the source already publishes; they add no new source claims.
missingNone: The source provides all of these.
conditionHint: Original-source conditions only; missing details do not match. These filters do not predict the best recipe for your beans.
equipmentIntro: Source-backed specifications, compatibility notes and related recipes for pour-over drippers, kettles, grinders and filters.
equipmentNote: Specifications follow official brand pages. Unspecified models are not guessed.
heroSubtitle: Explore original recipes. Find your next cup.
homeDescription: A free, nine-language library of source-backed pour-over recipes from leading coffee authors and competitors, with original sources, versions and verification dates.
quickAnswer: Quick answer: {dose} g ground coffee, {water} {unit} water, {temperature}, grind {grind}, total time {time}.
faqAmountQuestion: How much coffee and water does {recipe} use?
faqTemperatureQuestion: What water temperature and grind does {recipe} use?
author: Author
sectionIntro: Original methods, carefully sourced. Browse by equipment, explore an author, or compare recipes side by side.
limit: You can compare up to three recipes.
compareSubtitle: Original parameters, side by side. See the differences clearly.
compareNote: Units are preserved as published. Water volume in mL is not silently converted to mass in g.
compareEmpty: Choose recipes from the library to begin a comparison.
invalidSelection: Some recipes in this link are unavailable, duplicated or exceed the three-recipe limit. Only valid selections are shown.
sourceIntro: Every recipe links to its creator or a publishing partner. Versions remain separate; missing details are shown explicitly.
methodText: Measurements stay in their published units. Equipment filters find matching equipment, not a personal best recipe. Fixed amounts are not automatically scaled.
translationNote: Translations are independently prepared and terminology-checked. The linked original remains the reference; no creator endorsement is implied.
imageNote: Editorial images are AI-generated illustrations, not photographs supplied by the recipe authors.
independent: An independent coffee reference by imycc.

siteInfo.aboutIntro: A free, independent library of source-backed pour-over recipes and brewing equipment.
siteInfo.aboutPurpose: The library collects publicly published recipes from baristas, competition broadcasts and brands. Each entry keeps its original source, version and checking date so you can return to the maker's own method.
siteInfo.aboutPrinciples: We keep source units and unknowns visible, separate versions, and do not invent missing values or imply that one method is best.
siteInfo.aboutIndependence: This is an independent reference. It is not affiliated with recipe authors or equipment brands, and trademarks remain with their owners.
siteInfo.contributeText: You can suggest recipes, report broken links, correct equipment facts or improve translations through the project repository.
siteInfo.termsIntro: Basic conditions for using this free recipe library.
siteInfo.termsUse: You may use the recipes for personal brewing and learning. Content is provided as it is, without a promise that it is complete, current or suitable for your equipment.
siteInfo.termsAccuracy: Recipes and equipment facts are checked against linked sources, but errors and source changes can happen. Check the original source and manufacturer instructions for important details.
siteInfo.termsResponsibility: Use care when handling hot water, blades, electricity and coffee equipment. This site is not legal, medical or safety advice.
siteInfo.termsRights: Recipe authors, publishers and equipment brands keep their own rights. Names and trademarks are used only to identify sources and products.
siteInfo.privacyIntro: This site is designed to avoid unnecessary data collection.
siteInfo.privacyData: There are no accounts, comment forms or newsletter sign-ups, so the site does not ask for your name, email address or payment details.
siteInfo.privacyAnalytics: Page views use GoatCounter, which records anonymous, aggregate visit information. See GoatCounter's privacy policy for current details.
siteInfo.privacyExternal: Source, video, GitHub and analytics sites have their own policies. Review them before sharing information with those services.

authorsIntro: Explore each author’s published recipes and original sources.
noResults: No recipes match these filters. Try another brewer or clear the filters.
raoWater: The source gives its own preferred figures, without a stated reporting basis.
raoPrep: With the valve open, rinse the filter and drain the rinse water. Fit the barrel firmly, add the coffee and level the bed.
derived: Total water is calculated from the source’s dose and stated mass ratio, not a separately published measurement.

instruction.bloom: Add the stated amount to wet the coffee grounds.
instruction.pour: Add the stated amount at the indicated time. The total so far is shown separately.
instruction.pause: Stop pouring until the next step begins.
instruction.close: Close the valve immediately after the first pour.
instruction.open: Open the valve after topping up.
instruction.topup: Pour until the water sits about 1 cm above the grounds.
instruction.pulses: Use short pours to keep the water 1–2 cm above the grounds, continuing to the total water target.
instruction.level: Level the coffee bed before brewing.
instruction.drain: Stop pouring and let the water level drop a little.

kodama.title: Hiroyuki Kodama · ORIGAMI Air
kodama.summary: Four pours with Wave paper and C40 MK4.
kodama.notes: 320 g water; approximately 265 g beverage. Total time is unspecified.
kodama.finish: Remove just before dripping stops; about 265 g beverage. No fixed time.
kodama.prep: Rinse with cold water. Grind 28 g at 25 clicks, remove fines using Saza M and blow off chaff. Use 21 g of prepared grounds.
kodama.water: Tajima natural water supplied at the event.

kobayashi.title: Tsuyoshi Kobayashi · ORIGAMI S
kobayashi.summary: Wave paper, Red Clix and a cooler final pour.
kobayashi.notes: 2024 third place. First round: 56 Red Clix clicks; final: 55. Last pour: approximately 75°C.
kobayashi.finish: Remove at 2:30 and mix gently with a spoon.
kobayashi.prep: Grind at 55 Red Clix clicks and sift to obtain 15 g. Rinse and fit the paper into the grooves with a pin, preheat the bowl and level the bed with a pin.
kobayashi.first: Pour gently and evenly over the bed.
kobayashi.last: Lower kettle water to approximately 75°C; use a thin, slow centre pour.
kobayashi.water: Tajima natural water was provided at the venue; the reporting basis for the hardness is not given.

selorio.title: Lui Selorio · ORIGAMI Air
selorio.summary: Four timed pours with ZP6 Special and CAFEC paper.
selorio.notes: Overview: 240 mL; steps: g. Third interval says 1:00–1:00, so only the start time is retained.
selorio.third: Start at 1:00; the third interval end is unclear in the source.
selorio.s00: Pour 50 g of water over ten seconds, then wait until 0:30.
selorio.s01: Pour 70 g of water over ten seconds, then wait until 1:00.
selorio.s03: Pour the last 60 g over ten seconds and let the water draw down until 2:25.

rincon.title: Janer Joseph Perez Rincon · ORIGAMI
rincon.summary: Natural Geisha with Sibarist and varying water temperatures.
rincon.notes: Exact pour times, first temperature, roast and total time are unspecified. Later temperatures are shown per step.
rincon.water: Source: Pure Colombian Water; mineral composition unspecified.
rincon.s00: First pour: 50 g of water. The card gives no temperature or time for this pour.
rincon.s01: Second pour: 70 g of water at 92 °C; no time is published.

gil.title: Milo Gil · ORIGAMI Air
gil.summary: Four pours with K-Ultra and Sibarist.
gil.notes: 2024 Dutch champion version. Sibarist model, beans and roast are unspecified. The source suggests about 7 g/s.
gil.s00: Start with a gentle pour of 40 g.
gil.s01: At 0:45 follow up with a pour of 60 g.
gil.s02: At 1:30 continue with a steady pour of 75 g.
gil.s03: At 2:15 conclude with a final pour of 75 g; the card suggests about 7 g/s and drawdown finishing near 3:00.

kasuya.title: Kasuya’s 4:6 method
kasuya.summary: Five pours, clearly timed. The HARIO-published version of Tetsu Kasuya’s 4:6 method.
kasuya.notes: This is HARIO’s published teaching version, not a reconstruction of the competition brew. Its last two pours begin at 2:10 and 2:40.
kasuya.finish: Remove the dripper at the source’s stated finish time.
kasuya.s00: Pour 50 mL at 0:00 — the source calls this 42% of the 120 mL first stage, or 40% of the total, favouring sweetness.
kasuya.s01: Add 70 mL at 0:45, topping the first stage up to 120 mL — the other 40% of the total.
kasuya.s02: Pour 60 mL at 1:30 — the remaining 180 mL is divided by the source into three equal pours.
kasuya.s03: Pour 60 mL at 2:10, the second of the three equal pours.

hoffmann.title: A better one-cup V60
hoffmann.summary: A small-batch V60 with measured pours, gentle swirls and short pauses.
hoffmann.notes: Freshly boiled water is the recommendation for lighter roasts. The finish time is approximate; the source prioritizes taste over a fixed drawdown time.
hoffmann.finish: Let the water drain through. Some variation in total time is expected.
hoffmann.s00: Pour 50 g of water to bloom.
hoffmann.s02: Pour up to 100 g total between 0:45 and 1:00 — 40% of the total weight.
hoffmann.s04: Pour up to 150 g total between 1:10 and 1:20 — 60% of the total weight.
hoffmann.s06: Pour up to 200 g total between 1:30 and 1:40 — 80% of the total weight.
hoffmann.s08: Pour up to 250 g total between 1:50 and 2:00 — the full weight.
hoffmann.s09: Gently swirl again for five seconds.

rao.title: Pulsar starting recipe
rao.summary: Valve-controlled blooming and short pulse pours for the NextLevel Pulsar.
rao.grind: Coarser than hand pour, finer than batch brew
rao.notes: The source outline gives a 45–60 second bloom, while its detailed technique resumes at 45–50 seconds. Both are retained here. Pulse amounts and exact later times are not specified.
rao.finish: The target total brew time is a range. Finish draining within that range as described by the source.
rao.s00: With the valve open, pour 75 g of water just off the boil.
rao.s01: Close the valve immediately so the grounds stay submerged.
rao.s02: At 45–50 seconds, pour enough water to raise the slurry about 1 cm above the grounds.
rao.s04: Pour in several short bursts, keeping the slurry 1–2 cm above the grounds, to the 425 g total.
rao.s05: Swirl the Pulsar gently immediately after the last pour.

licata.title: Continuous-pour V60
licata.summary: A forceful start, a slower centre pour, and a turbulent final addition.
licata.notes: Uses light-roasted Colombia La Palma y El Tucan natural Gesha. The intermediate 250 mL total is calculated by subtracting the final 50 mL from the total. Intermediate phase times are unspecified.
licata.bloom: Wet the grounds and bloom for 30 seconds.
licata.continuous: Start with a fast, forceful pour, then slow to a centre pour until the cumulative target of 250 mL.
licata.finalPour: Add the final 50 mL quickly to create turbulence.
licata.beans: Light-roasted Colombia La Palma y El Tucan natural Gesha
licata.water: Its unit and reporting basis are not stated.

wong.title: Switch steep and release
wong.summary: Begin with open-valve percolation, then steep and release.
wong.notes: The source says hot water without a temperature or composition. The second addition of 110 g is calculated from the 140 g total minus the 30 g bloom.
wong.finish: At 4:00, close the valve and remove the dripper.
wong.s01: With the valve open, bloom with 30 g of water from 0:00 to 0:10.
wong.s02: Pour to 140 g total between 0:40 and 0:55; the 110 g addition is that target minus the 30 g bloom.
wong.s04: At 1:15 close the valve and pour to 240 g; the 100 g addition is the remaining water.

boen.title: Two-stage Switch immersion
boen.summary: Two closed-valve steeps combined with open-valve percolation.
boen.notes: HARIO’s published 2021 World Brewers Cup recipe. The overview specifies 240 mL, while the steps use g. This discrepancy is preserved without equating the units.
boen.finish: Drain after opening the valve; target a total of 3:00–3:15.
boen.open: Open at 0:40 and immediately start the next pour.
boen.centre: Pour the stated amount into the centre.
boen.circle: Add the stated amount in a circular pattern.
boen.beans: Natural Geisha from Hacienda La Esmeralda
boen.s01: With the dripper closed, pour 50 g of water for the bloom and leave it for 40 seconds.

hoang.title: Dual-filter W60
hoang.summary: A flat mesh bed and paper filter with three water additions.
hoang.notes: HARIO’s published 2021 World Brewers Cup recipe. The overview gives 200 g, but the steps use mL. Both are preserved without assuming equivalence.
hoang.water: It is not stated whether the figure is hardness or total dissolved solids.
hoang.filters: W60 flat mesh and paper filter used together.
hoang.prep: The author recommends sifting out fines before brewing.
hoang.s00: Bloom with 50 mL of water for 30 seconds.
hoang.s01: Pour another 100 mL of water over 30 seconds.
hoang.s02: Pour the final 50 mL of water at 2:00.

rojewska.title: Fast two-stage V60
rojewska.summary: Gentle circular pouring followed by a fast centre pour.
rojewska.notes: The listed 1:00 is the end of pouring; the total target is 2:15. Bloom amount and temperature are unspecified. The 150 mL is a cumulative target, not a post-bloom addition.
rojewska.finish: Stop pouring around 1:00 and let drain; target a total of 2:15.
rojewska.bloom: Pre-infuse for 15 seconds; the water amount is unspecified.
rojewska.circle: Pour gently in circles to a cumulative 150 mL, including the pre-infusion water.
rojewska.centre: Add the remaining 100 mL quickly in the centre, maintaining the water level; stop around 1:00.

grill.title: Martha Grill’s morning V60
grill.summary: A 30 g V60 with a 30-second bloom, two pours and a finish at three minutes.
grill.notes: The published recipe uses 30 g coffee and 500 mL at 92°C. Its instructions use g for the pour targets, so those units are preserved separately. The article names Ézio Sartori coffee from Brazil but does not name a grind setting.
grill.beans: Ézio Sartori, Espírito Santo, Brazil; roasted by Coffee Lab
grill.s00: Pour 60 g of water and let it bloom for 30 seconds.
grill.s01: On the second pour go to 250 g; the 190 g addition is that target minus the bloom.
grill.s03: At 1:30 pour the rest of the water, taking the total to 500 g.

mallouhi.title: Ibrahim Al Mallouhi’s V60
mallouhi.summary: A 1:15 V60 with a 40 mL circular bloom and a slow remaining pour.
mallouhi.notes: The source states 20 g coffee, 300 mL water and a 2:10 target, but does not specify water temperature.
mallouhi.finish: Target a total brew time of 2:10.
mallouhi.prep: Pre-wet the filter and discard the rinse water before adding coffee.
mallouhi.water: The source says hot water but does not provide a temperature.
mallouhi.s00: Slowly pour 40 mL of hot water in circular motions, then let it bloom for 35 seconds.
mallouhi.s01: Slowly pour the remaining water — 260 mL, the published 300 mL less the bloom — in small circular motions.

chronicler.title: Coffee Chronicler Switch recipe
chronicler.summary: A two-pour Switch recipe: half the water open, half steeped, then released.
chronicler.notes: The article’s standard version uses 20 g coffee and 320 g water: pour half with the valve open, close at 0:45, add the remaining half, then open at 2:00. Temperature and grind are not specified.
chronicler.finish: Let the brew drain; the article gives a 2:45–3:15 total range.
chronicler.open: Start with the Switch valve open.
chronicler.firstPour: Pour the first half of the water while the valve is open.
chronicler.close: Close the valve at 0:45 for the steep.
chronicler.secondPour: Add the remaining half of the water, then steep.
chronicler.drain: Open at 2:00 and let the brew drain.

hoffmann-ultimate.title: The ultimate V60 technique
hoffmann-ultimate.summary: A 30 g V60 recipe with a 60 g bloom, staged pours to 500 g and a final stir.
hoffmann-ultimate.notes: The source recommends water as hot as possible, especially for lighter roasts. The finish time is a target; drawdown varies with paper and temperature.
hoffmann-ultimate.finish: Let the brew draw down, aiming to finish around 3:30.
hoffmann-ultimate.s00: At t = 0:00 add twice the coffee weight, 60 g of bloom water.
hoffmann-ultimate.s01: Swirl the slurry until evenly mixed so all grounds are wetted — the source prefers swirling to a spoon here.
hoffmann-ultimate.s02: Bloom for up to 45 seconds, then add 240 g over the next 30 seconds to reach 300 g, 60% of the total brew weight.
hoffmann-ultimate.s03: Add the last 200 g over 30 seconds to reach 500 g, a little slower than the previous phase and not too aggressively.
hoffmann-ultimate.s04: At t = 1:45 stir once clockwise with a spoon.
hoffmann-ultimate.s05: Then stir once anticlockwise with the spoon.
hoffmann-ultimate.s06: Allow the V60 to drain a little.
hoffmann-ultimate.s07: Give the V60 a gentle swirl, then let it draw down — the source aims to finish by 3:30.

camber.title: Camber Coffee V60
camber.summary: A 20 g V60 recipe with a 60 g bloom and two pours to 345 g, shared for anaerobic coffees.
camber.notes: The source recommends this recipe for anaerobic processed coffees. Water temperature is not stated.
camber.finish: Aim for a total brew time of 3:00–3:15.
camber.bean: The source recommends anaerobic processed coffees.
camber.s00: Bloom with 60 g of water between 0:00 and 0:30.
camber.s01: Pour up to 200 g between 0:30 and 0:45.
camber.s02: At 1:00 make the final pour up to 345 g.

lamill.title: LAMILL V60 Mugen
lamill.summary: A 16.5 g one-pour Mugen recipe with 225 g water and a 3:00–3:30 drawdown.
lamill.notes: The source uses no bloom or temperature specification; it asks for one continuous concentric pour finishing at 0:40.
lamill.finish: Allow the bed to draw down, aiming for 3:00–3:30.
lamill.prepare: Pre-wet the filter, add 16.5 g of coffee and make a small crater in the centre.
lamill.s00: Start the timer and pour all 225 g in concentric circles from the centre slowly outward, finishing this single pour at 0:40.
